# Meeting Templates Collection

## Overview

Effective meetings are crucial for project success. This collection provides structured templates for common project meetings to ensure they are focused, productive, and achieve their intended outcomes.

**Purpose**: Provide standardized formats and agendas for essential project meetings

**When to Use**: Throughout all project phases for regular and ad-hoc meetings

**Who Uses**: Project Managers, Team Members, Stakeholders

---

## Meeting Types Included

### 1. Project Kickoff Meeting
### 2. Weekly Team Meeting
### 3. Sprint Planning Meeting
### 4. Sprint Review Meeting
### 5. Sprint Retrospective
### 6. Stakeholder Review Meeting
### 7. Risk Review Meeting
### 8. Change Control Board Meeting
### 9. Project Steering Committee Meeting
### 10. Daily Standup Meeting

---

## 1. Project Kickoff Meeting Template

### Meeting Information
- **Meeting Title**: [Project Name] Kickoff Meeting
- **Date**: [Date]
- **Time**: [Start Time] - [End Time] ([Duration])
- **Location**: [Physical/Virtual Location]
- **Meeting Type**: Project Kickoff
- **Meeting Owner**: [Project Manager]
- **Facilitator**: [Name]
- **Note Taker**: [Name]

### Attendees
**Required Attendees**:
- [ ] Project Manager
- [ ] Project Sponsor
- [ ] Core Team Members
- [ ] Key Stakeholders

**Optional Attendees**:
- [ ] Subject Matter Experts
- [ ] Extended Team Members

### Pre-Meeting Preparation
**Send to Attendees 3 Days Before**:
- [ ] Project Charter
- [ ] High-level project schedule
- [ ] Team contact list
- [ ] Meeting agenda

**Prepare Materials**:
- [ ] Project overview presentation
- [ ] Roles and responsibilities document
- [ ] Communication plan draft
- [ ] Risk register (initial)

### Meeting Agenda

| Time | Duration | Topic | Owner | Outcome |
|------|----------|-------|-------|---------|
| [Time] | 5 min | Welcome & Introductions | PM | All participants introduced |
| [Time] | 15 min | Project Overview | Sponsor | Shared understanding of purpose |
| [Time] | 20 min | Project Charter Review | PM | Charter approved/signed |
| [Time] | 15 min | Scope & Deliverables | PM | Clear scope understanding |
| [Time] | 10 min | Timeline & Milestones | PM | Schedule awareness |
| [Time] | 10 min | Roles & Responsibilities | PM | Clear role definitions |
| [Time] | 10 min | Communication Plan | PM | Communication agreements |
| [Time] | 10 min | Success Criteria | PM | Shared success vision |
| [Time] | 5 min | Next Steps & Actions | PM | Clear action items |
| [Time] | 5 min | Q&A | All | Issues resolved |

**Total Duration**: 105 minutes (1 hour 45 minutes)

### Key Discussion Points
1. **Project Purpose & Business Case**
   - Why are we doing this project?
   - What problems are we solving?
   - What are the expected benefits?

2. **Project Scope**
   - What is included in the project?
   - What is explicitly excluded?
   - What are the key deliverables?

3. **Team Structure**
   - Who is on the team?
   - What are their roles and responsibilities?
   - How will decisions be made?

4. **Project Approach**
   - What methodology will we use?
   - What are our key processes?
   - How will we handle changes?

5. **Communication & Collaboration**
   - How will we communicate?
   - What tools will we use?
   - How often will we meet?

### Action Items Template
| Action Item | Assigned To | Due Date | Status | Notes |
|-------------|-------------|----------|--------|-------|
| [Action description] | [Name] | [Date] | [Status] | [Notes] |

### Success Criteria
- [ ] All team members understand project purpose and goals
- [ ] Roles and responsibilities are clearly defined
- [ ] Communication plan is agreed upon
- [ ] Initial risks are identified
- [ ] Next steps are defined with owners and dates

## 5. Sprint Retrospective Template

### Meeting Information
- **Meeting Title**: Sprint [#] Retrospective
- **Date**: [Date]
- **Time**: [Start Time] - [End Time]
- **Location**: [Physical/Virtual Location]
- **Facilitator**: [Scrum Master]

### Attendees
**Required**:
- [ ] Development Team
- [ ] Scrum Master
- [ ] Product Owner (optional)

### Meeting Agenda

| Time | Duration | Topic | Method | Outcome |
|------|----------|-------|--------|---------|
| [Time] | 5 min | Check-in | Round robin | Team engagement |
| [Time] | 15 min | What Went Well | Appreciation circle | Positive reinforcement |
| [Time] | 15 min | What Didn't Go Well | Problem identification | Issue awareness |
| [Time] | 15 min | What We Learned | Insight sharing | Knowledge capture |
| [Time] | 15 min | What to Try Next | Action planning | Improvement commitments |
| [Time] | 5 min | Closing & Actions | Summary | Clear next steps |

**Total Duration**: 70 minutes

### Retrospective Techniques

**Technique 1: Start-Stop-Continue**
- **Start**: What should we start doing?
- **Stop**: What should we stop doing?
- **Continue**: What should we continue doing?

**Technique 2: Mad-Sad-Glad**
- **Mad**: What frustrated us?
- **Sad**: What disappointed us?
- **Glad**: What made us happy?

**Technique 3: 4 L's**
- **Liked**: What did we like?
- **Learned**: What did we learn?
- **Lacked**: What did we lack?
- **Longed For**: What did we long for?

## 10. Daily Standup Meeting Template

### Meeting Information
- **Meeting Title**: Daily Standup
- **Time**: [Same time daily]
- **Duration**: 15 minutes maximum
- **Location**: [Consistent location]
- **Facilitator**: [Scrum Master/Team Lead]

### Attendees
**Required**:
- [ ] Development Team
- [ ] Scrum Master/Team Lead

**Optional**:
- [ ] Product Owner
- [ ] Stakeholders (observers only)

### Meeting Format

**For Each Team Member** (2-3 minutes each):
1. **What did I complete yesterday?**
   - Focus on work items completed
   - Connect to sprint/project goals

2. **What will I work on today?**
   - Specific tasks or objectives
   - Commitment for the day

3. **Do I have any blockers or impediments?**
   - Obstacles preventing progress
   - Help needed from team

### Facilitator Guidelines
- **Keep it time-boxed**: Maximum 15 minutes
- **Stay focused**: Three questions only
- **Address blockers**: Note impediments for follow-up
- **Encourage collaboration**: Team coordination
- **Avoid problem-solving**: Take detailed discussions offline

### Common Anti-Patterns to Avoid
- ❌ Status reporting to the manager
- ❌ Detailed problem-solving discussions
- ❌ Long explanations of technical details
- ❌ Blame or criticism
- ❌ Missing team members regularly

### Follow-Up Actions
- [ ] Schedule detailed discussions for blockers
- [ ] Update project tracking tools
- [ ] Communicate impediments to stakeholders
- [ ] Adjust daily plans based on team input

---

## Meeting Best Practices

### General Guidelines

#### Before the Meeting
- [ ] Send agenda 24-48 hours in advance
- [ ] Include all necessary background materials
- [ ] Confirm attendee availability
- [ ] Test technology and equipment
- [ ] Prepare materials and handouts

#### During the Meeting
- [ ] Start and end on time
- [ ] Follow the agenda
- [ ] Encourage participation from all attendees
- [ ] Take clear notes and action items
- [ ] Summarize key decisions and next steps

#### After the Meeting
- [ ] Send meeting notes within 24 hours
- [ ] Distribute action items with owners and due dates
- [ ] Update project documentation
- [ ] Schedule follow-up meetings as needed
- [ ] File meeting records appropriately

### Virtual Meeting Tips
- [ ] Test technology before the meeting
- [ ] Use video when possible
- [ ] Mute when not speaking
- [ ] Share screens effectively
- [ ] Use collaboration tools (polls, whiteboard)
- [ ] Take frequent engagement checks

### Meeting Effectiveness Measures
- **Attendance Rate**: [Target: >90%]
- **On-Time Start**: [Target: 100%]
- **Action Item Completion**: [Target: >85%]
- **Meeting Duration**: [Target: Within scheduled time]
- **Participant Satisfaction**: [Survey quarterly]

## When to Use

Use throughout the project lifecycle to identify, assess, and track risks. This template is essential for projects with significant complexity, multiple stakeholders, or high business impact, where structured risk management provides decision-making value.

## When NOT to Use

Do not use for very low-risk, short-duration tasks where informal risk awareness is sufficient. Avoid this template if your governance framework requires a different risk management approach or if stakeholders prefer real-time risk dashboards over static registers.

## Customization Guidelines

### Adapt for Your Organization
1. **Add company-specific formats** and branding
2. **Include required attendees** per company policy
3. **Align with existing meeting standards** and tools
4. **Incorporate organizational terminology**

### Scale for Project Size
- **Small Projects**: Use shorter, informal versions
- **Medium Projects**: Use standard templates
- **Large Projects**: Add additional governance meetings

### Methodology Alignment
- **Traditional PM**: Formal agendas and documentation
- **Agile PM**: Shorter, more frequent meetings
- **Hybrid PM**: Mix formal and informal based on context
